title: Sales Enablement Playbook: Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pitch Decks, Pricing & Security FAQ
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's core sales enablement artifacts for prospect-facing conversations: our positioning and messaging, competitive battlecards, pitch deck guidance, pricing guidance and negotiation levers, short case studies with measurable outcomes, and a security FAQ tailored for prospects evaluating hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Use this as the canonical single-page reference when preparing demos, proposals, or executive briefings.

Key use-cases and owners
- Primary users: AEs, SDRs, Solutions Engineers, Customer Success Managers, Sales Engineers.
- Owner: Go-to-market (content maintained by Product Marketing + Sales Engineering).
- Update cadence: Quarterly review; immediate updates after major product launches or pricing changes.

1) Positioning & Core Messages
- Headline positioning (elevator): Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that makes LLM-powered features predictable, cost-effective, and reliable across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

- 3-line pitch:
  1. For engineering-led product teams, Redwood provides a consistent API and operational tooling to serve LLMs with production SLAs and transparent unit economics.
  2. We optimize inference throughput and cost via batching, caching, and quantization profiles while preserving output quality.
  3. Customers can choose hosted, reserved (Dedicated), or private (VPC/on-prem) deployments without re-architecting their application.

- Differentiators to emphasize (talk tracks):
  - Production-first: measurable SLOs (99.9% uptime targets on Dedicated) and per-route latency percentiles for predictable UX.
  - Unified runtime: same API/rollout model across environments reduces integration debt.
  - Cost control levers: automated batching, KV/prefix caching, and model/quantization recommendations that show unit cost reductions typically in the 30-60% range versus naive per-request serving.
  - Reliability & graceful fallback: automatic routing by policy and model-variant fallbacks to maintain availability under capacity constraints.

- Persona-specific messaging
  - CTO / VP Eng: focus on operational risk, SLAs, private deployments, multi-region, and vendor lock-in minimization. Bring up audit logs, KMS/HSM integrations, and upgrade rollbacks.
  - ML/Infra Lead: focus on serving runtime performance, kernel selection, quantization profiles, batching tradeoffs, and profiling/playbooks. Offer benchmarking results and open invitation to lab-run model onboarding.
  - Product Manager: focus on developer velocity, same API across environments, cost predictability, and ability to iterate on model versions with canary rollouts and A/B testing.
  - Procurement / Security: focus on compliance, SOC2/ISO posture (link to compliance evidence), and contract SLAs for Dedicated/Private.

2) Competitive Briefs (battlecards)
- Competitors covered: Cloud-managed ML endpoints (major cloud providers), LLM API providers (general marketplace), and inference infrastructure vendors (self-hosted runtimes).

- Battlecard format (one-pager to use in calls):
  - Competitor: [Name]
  - Typical strengths customers cite
  - Primary weaknesses to highlight (our counterpoints)
  - Questions to uncover buyer pain that favors Redwood
  - Recommended demo/script and red-team claims

- Example: Competitor — Cloud Provider Managed Endpoints
  - Strengths: integration with existing cloud accounts, simple single-command deployments, deep cloud ecosystem hooks.
  - Weaknesses: opaque unit economics for inference, limited quantization/optimized kernels for specific LLMs, weaker multi-environment parity between hosted and private.
  - Uncovering questions: "How predictable are your per-token costs during peak traffic? How do you handle private (air-gapped) deployments?)"
  - Demo/script: show our per-route token-level cost breakdown, routing policy editor, and Dedicated SLA terms.

- Competitive play: always probe for cost sensitivity, privatization needs, and multi-region requirements. Emphasize our measurable cost controls and operational tooling.

3) Pitch Deck Guidance & Slide Deck Template
- Core deck structure (10-14 slides recommended):
  1. Title & one-liner (customer logo if post-prospect)
  2. The problem we solve (latency, cost, reliability, deployment friction)
  3. Why now (open models + model sprawl + production economics)
  4. What Redwood does (platform overview: hosted, Dedicated, Private)
  5. How it works (serving runtime, smart routing, caching/ batching)
  6. Key differentiators (production-first, unified runtime, cost controls)
  7. Architecture options (hosted, dedicated reserved pools, private VPC/on-prem) — include recommended deployment for the prospect
  8. Performance / benchmark highlights (p50/p95 latency, throughput metrics for relevant models)
  9. Pricing & commercial options (high-level)
  10. Case study / customer outcomes (relevant industry example)
  11. Security & compliance (SOC2, KMS, audit logs)
  12. Next steps & recommended PoC scope

- Slide tactics and evidence to include
  - Always include sample latency percentiles (p50/p95) and per-route cost breakdowns for a representative workload.
  - Use a one-slide demo transcript: API call -> streaming response -> tracing -> cost analysis.
  - For technical buyers include a short architecture diagram showing KV cache, batching, and model variant fallback.

- Demo checklist for SEs (pre-call prep)
  1. Create a demo API key scoped to a sandbox project.
  2. Load a representative prompt set and enable streaming.
  3. Precompute a small quantization profile example (if discussing quantization).
  4. Prepare cost dashboard screenshot for a sample 100k-token/day workload.
  5. Have backup plans: a recorded demo video and an offline deck in case of network issues.

4) Pricing Guidance & Negotiation Levers
- Pricing models we use:
  - Hosted API: usage-based pricing (per-token generation and per-embedding unit).
  - Redwood Dedicated: committed reserved capacity with monthly/annual commit tiers for predictable throughput; overage and burst pricing documented in SOW.
  - Redwood Private: platform license + support/maintenance fee; optional engineering services for on-prem onboarding.

- How to position pricing by buyer profile
  - Early-stage / PLG adoption customers: lead with Hosted API to reduce friction; offer trial credits and a clear path to Dedicated once steady traffic emerges.
  - Mid-market: propose Dedicated with a 6-12 month commit and predictable unit pricing; include implementation services as needed.
  - Enterprise / Regulated: Private deployment plus a multi-year support agreement; include compliance add-ons and higher SLAs.

- List of standard contract levers for negotiation (for Sales + Legal)
  - Commit term and volume discounts (Dedicated only).
  - Minimum revenue guarantees vs shorter ramp schedules.
  - Pilot terms: 30-90 day pilot with capped consumption and optional conversion credits.
  - Professional services: fixed-fee onboarding or hourly.
  - Enhanced observability retention and premium SLA as add-ons.

- Pricing objection scripts
  - Objection: "It's more expensive than our current provider." Response: "Can we walk through a realistic monthly token profile? Most customers find our cost controls (batching/caching/quantization) reduce the effective per-request cost. We can run a free workload analysis and show estimated unit cost impact."

5) Case Studies (two concise vignettes for sales use)
- Case study: SaaS search vendor (Mid-market)
  - Problem: search relevance pipeline lagged due to high per-request latency and cost at scale.
  - Solution: migrated to Redwood Dedicated, enabled KV prefix caching, and implemented model quantization profile.
  - Outcome: 45% reduction in inference cost per query, p95 latency dropped from 420ms to 180ms, and mean time to rollback a model version reduced from 3 hours to 20 minutes using canary rollouts.
  - Key quote: "Redwood gave us predictable performance and cut our inference spend in half while improving UX." — Head of Engineering, AcmeSearch

- Case study: Regulated financial services (Enterprise)
  - Problem: regulatory constraints required on-prem model serving and auditability.
  - Solution: Private deployment with customer-managed KMS and audit logging, plus a 3-month on-prem onboarding engagement.
  - Outcome: achieved required audit posture, maintained equivalent latency to cloud-hosted baselines, and enabled secure model versioning for compliance.
  - Key quote: "Redwood's private deployment path let us use modern LLMs without compromising our compliance requirements." — Director of ML, FinBank

6) Security FAQ for Prospects (concise answers for sales teams)
- Q: What compliance certifications does Redwood maintain?
  A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and is pursuing ISO 27001. We provide compliance evidence packages to enterprise customers under NDA.

- Q: Where is customer data stored and can you support data residency?
  A: Hosted data is stored in region-specific cloud accounts; customers can select region for data residency. Dedicated and Private options support VPC and on-prem deployments for stricter residency requirements.

- Q: How is encryption managed in transit and at rest?
  A: All network traffic is TLS 1.2+/TLS 1.3. Data at rest is encrypted using provider-managed encryption keys by default; Dedicated and Private customers can provide their own KMS/HSM keys.

- Q: Do you support customer-managed keys (CMKs) and HSM integrations?
  A: Yes — Dedicated and Private customers can integrate with common KMS providers and HSMs. We support bring-your-own-key for auditability.

- Q: How do you handle model provenance and versioning?
  A: The platform exposes model version identifiers, rollout history, and immutable audit logs that record which model version served each request. We support canary rollouts and automated rollback policies.

- Q: What controls do customers have for data retention and deletion?
  A: Customers can configure retention windows and request deletion. Private and Dedicated deployments can be configured to not persist logs beyond customer-defined retention.

- Q: How do you mitigate data exfiltration risk from generated outputs?
  A: We provide output filtering hooks, redaction tooling, and per-route content policies. For high-sensitivity customers, we recommend Private deployment with on-prem inference and constrained model access.

- Q: What are the incident response and disclosure practices?
  A: We maintain an incident response playbook aligned with industry best practices and will notify customers based on contractual SLAs. Security incidents are documented in post-incident reports and shared with affected customers per our incident disclosure policy.

7) Objection Handling & Discovery Questions
- Common objections and rebuttals
  - "We can self-host cheaper." -> "Heard many teams say this; the true TCO includes engineering effort, reliability risk, and slower feature velocity. We offer benchmarking and a migration plan that clarifies the full picture."
  - "We're locked into cloud X." -> "We integrate with major cloud providers and can operate within existing accounts; Dedicated and Private options are built for multi-cloud or on-prem footprints."

- Discovery checklist to run during discovery calls
  1. Current monthly token/embedding volume and projected growth.
  2. Latency requirements (p50/p95 targets) by endpoint.
  3. Data residency and compliance constraints.
  4. Peak traffic patterns and burst tolerance.
  5. Current TCO estimates and any in-flight infra commitments.
  6. Decision makers and procurement timeline.

Appendix: Quick reference stats
- Typical cost savings with Redwood Optimize suggestions: 30-60% effective per-token cost reduction (customer-dependent).
- Dedicated SLA: 99.9% uptime target (negotiable in enterprise contracts).
- Common onboarding timeline: Hosted: <1 week; Dedicated: 4-8 weeks; Private: 8-16 weeks (includes on-prem engagements).

Maintenance notes
- Update this playbook after every pricing revision, major product release, or when new compliant evidence packages are onboarded.
- Send substantive changes to reviewers listed in metadata for signoff before publishing.
